title: Finalize tier principles + customer-facing reliability narrative (Hosted vs Dedicated)
creator: Talia Benson
project: Tiered SLO definitions + error budget policy
description:
Goal
Finalize the product-tier principles and customer-facing narrative for reliability (Hosted API vs Dedicated) so that:
1) Dedicated positioning matches operational reality (pool isolation + predictable throughput, but not “magically perfect latency”).
2) Customer-facing docs/support scripts align with the canonical SLO definitions + error budget policy.
3) Sales/CS and Support can answer “what do you do when things go wrong” consistently, without over-promising.

Background / problem
We’ve historically described Dedicated as “more reliable” without a crisp definition. As we roll out tiered SLOs + error budget enforcement, we need a short set of tier principles and a narrative that:
- clearly sets expectations about what Dedicated improves vs Hosted
- explains what the SLOs mean (and what they don’t)
- explains what Redwood does operationally when burn spikes (routing fallbacks, protective throttling, canary gates/change controls)
- avoids implying contractual SLA terms (handled separately)

Deliverables
A) Tier principles (internal, canonical)
- A 1-page principle set that can be re-used across docs, sales enablement, Support macros, and Console copy.
- Includes: what’s included/excluded for SLO reporting, and the intended “feel” of error budget enforcement.

B) Customer-facing narrative + copy blocks (Hosted + Dedicated)
- Short reliability statement for Hosted API (docs + Console tooltip usage)
- Short reliability statement for Dedicated (docs + console)
- FAQ: “SLO vs SLA”, “What happens if you run out of error budget?”, “What do you do during incidents?”, “How is Dedicated isolated?”, “What does ‘pool readiness’ mean?”

C) Alignment artifacts
- Support/CS talk track (bullet version) and escalation expectations by tier
- Status-page phrasing guidance (Hosted vs Dedicated impact wording)

Proposed tier principles (draft)
1) Hosted API = multi-tenant, breadth of models, best time-to-value
- Designed for fast onboarding, broad model catalog access, and elastic scale.
- Reliability is managed via global routing, fallbacks to compatible variants, and protective mechanisms (rate limiting/throttling) to keep the platform stable under stress.
- Performance is defined per endpoint class (streaming chat/completions vs embeddings), and customers should expect some variance by model/region.

2) Dedicated = reserved, isolated capacity with predictable throughput + operational guardrails
- Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools with data isolation and predictable baseline throughput.
- Dedicated does not mean “no incidents”; it means better isolation from multi-tenant load and clearer capacity commitments.
- Dedicated SLOs include pool readiness/capacity signals in addition to request SLIs; these reflect operational reality (autoscaling/provisioning lag, dependency failures).

3) SLOs are targets used to drive engineering behavior (not contractual guarantees)
- SLOs define how Redwood measures reliability and prioritizes work.
- SLA terms (if any) are separate and contract-specific.

4) Error budgets are the steering wheel
- When burn is healthy: normal change velocity with progressive rollouts.
- When burn is at risk: tighten rollout policies, reduce blast radius (canary-only), require additional approvals.
- When exhausted: change freeze for non-mitigation changes, rollback/mitigation prioritized, and automated protective behavior may activate.

5) We prefer graceful degradation over hard failure
- Hosted: fallbacks + protective throttling are acceptable to maintain overall availability and prevent cascading failures.
- Dedicated: fallbacks are constrained to what is explicitly allowed for that customer/pool; where fallbacks are not allowed, we prioritize pool recovery and transparent comms.

6) Clear exclusions and attribution
- Exclusions must be explicit (invalid auth, malformed requests, customer-side disconnects/timeouts where applicable).
- Streaming disconnect attribution must be explained in plain language (client abort vs server-side disconnect).

Open questions to resolve in this ticket
- Dedicated messaging: how explicit do we get about “autoscaling/provision-to-ready lag”? (Proposed: mention “capacity readiness” as a measured indicator; keep implementation detail out of customer docs.)
- Hosted messaging: how to describe protective throttling without sounding like we randomly drop traffic? (Proposed: “temporary protective limits to preserve platform stability; customers receive 429/503 with retry guidance.”)
- Fallback language: what’s safe to promise for Dedicated? (Proposed: “only within customer-approved compatibility set; otherwise no silent model swaps.”)

Acceptance criteria
- Tier principles approved by: SRE (Sean/Rafael), Platform (Priya/Ethan), Routing (Mina/Ravi), Support/CS escalation owner (Dev Patel).
- Copy blocks delivered to Docs team (Elliot Price / Wei Chen / Kira Thompson) and included in internal enablement notes.
- Support macro + escalation talk track drafted and reviewed by Owen Phillips + Rachel Kim.
- Links added to PM-612 (Console requirements) so UI strings align.

comments: 2026-01-16 — Lauren Bishop: Drafted first pass of tier principles (v0). Biggest concern: Dedicated expectations are currently set by sales decks implying p99 guarantees; we need explicit language that Dedicated = reserved capacity + isolation, not “always low latency.” Requesting input from Rafael on what we can confidently target for p99 in Dedicated without constant exception handling.

2026-01-20 — Nikhil Sharma: Proposed Hosted narrative emphasis: reliability comes from routing + graceful degradation, and the platform may enforce temporary protective limits to prevent cascading failure. Need wording that’s honest but not scary; will sync with Support for common “why am I seeing 429/503?” questions.

2026-01-22 — Rafael Mendes: From SRE POV, we should avoid committing to specific mitigations in customer-facing docs (e.g., “we will always fallback to X”). Better: describe classes of mitigations and that they are tier-aware. Dedicated: call out that fallbacks are policy-controlled and may be disabled for strict isolation customers.

2026-02-05 — Marissa Cole: Reviewed proposed copy blocks for Console tooltips; request: keep the customer-facing narrative tight, then link to deeper reliability docs for power users. Also ensure that “SLO vs SLA” FAQ is prominent to reduce contract confusion.

2026-02-11 — Dev Patel: Support wants a simple rubric: Hosted incidents = broad impact messaging, “mitigations may include throttling”; Dedicated escalations = include pool name/region/model in intake, mention readiness/capacity signal, and expectations for comms cadence. Please add a 5-bullet talk track we can convert into macros.

2026-02-18 — Rachel Kim: Enterprise comms note: don’t say “error budget exhausted” externally. We can say “we are operating under heightened change control while we restore service stability.” Also clarify that Dedicated customers get proactive updates when their pool readiness is degraded (even if request SLI looks fine).

2026-02-21 — Lauren Bishop: Incorporated feedback. Final principles + copy blocks sent to Elliot/Wei/Kira for docs integration. Added explicit constraint: Dedicated model fallback only within customer-approved compatibility set; no silent swaps for strict-isolation pools. Marking Done after SRE/Platform sign-off in today’s sync.
